items.name: An Introduction to Jewelcrafting
items.notes:
No longer in the game. 
Step 1. Determine the appropriate gemstone
grade for your metal type using our nifty pairing
chart!

               Copper = Chipped
               Bronze = Flawed
               Silver = Flawed
               Iron = Imperfect
               Gold = Imperfect
               Steel = Normal
               Platinum = Normal
               Mithril = Flawless

Step 2. Determine the required components for
your jewelry. Keep in mind that each component
must be made from the same metal type. No
mixing and matching!

Ring
- 1 Gemstone
- 1 Setting
- 1 Wire

Earring
- 1 Gemstone
- 1 Mounting
- 1 Wire

Necklace
- 1 Gemstone
- 1 Chain Links
- 1 Mounting
- 1 Wire

Step 3. Create the required components. If
you're not multi-talented, consider making
friends with a blacksmith and an enchanter!

Chain Links
- 4 Metal Bar

Mounting
- 1 Enchanted Metal Bar

Setting
- 2 Enchanted Metal Bar

Wire
- 1 Metal Bar

Step 4. Visit a Jewelcrafting Bench, or put it all
together inside a Jewelcrafting Kit and hope for
the best. Good luck!

items.name: Basics of Culinary Preparation
items.notes:
No longer sold at vendors 
Welcome to the wonderful world of culinary expression!

But before you can go forth on your path towards excellence, you will have to master the basics.

Many things in this world require a bit of refinement before they can be used. A sharpened and honed cleaver is all we need for most preparations, but solid mortar and pestle will be required for grinding spices and other such ingredients.

Many vegetables and herbs can be processed simply by chopping them with a cleaver. Place them on the counter and chop vigorously! If you have a lot of vegetables to chop, an experienced chef would suggest to take five of them at once, and chop them with gusto!

Meat, on the other hand, need to be refined from the rough chunks you can get from hunting or from meat sellers.

Simply take your chunk of meat and your cleaver, and cut it cleanly into two steaks.

Those steaks can then be chopped into meat chunks, and those chunks can be individually refined into minced meat.

Bon Appetit!

items.name: Hunter's Guide to Carnivorism
items.notes:
Greetings!

Are you tired of being almonished to eat your vegetables? Do you slay enough creatures to feed a small adventuring party? Do you want to get in touch with your true nature as a ravening beast that craves the flesh of the living?

If you answered yes, then this is the book for you! Enclosed within its pages are recipes for any aspiring meat-eater. Learn, and go forth, carnivore!

Creature-On-A-Stick

For this recipe, you will need a set of wooden skewers, some salt, and an unrefined piece of meat from an edible creature, like a rat or a bat. Salt it, place it on the skewer, and roast over the fire. You'll have a delicous animal on a stick in no time!

Roasted Creature

A slightly more advanced recipe. This requires a roasting spit, some salt, and a piece of meat. Salt the meat and place it on the spit. Soon, you will have a savory roast.

Basic Meat Handling

What, you didn't thick you could just slap some raw meat on a fire and be done with it? Okay, you could do that, actually, but what if you wanted to make something a little more advanced? Or maybe you just want to cut out some of that gristle?

Meat can be refined into steaks by carefully chopping it with a cleaver. More marginal meats, like rat meat, will only produce chunks... but who wants to eat rat steak, anyway? (You do. Because you're carnivore. Steaks can then be cut into chunks, and those chunks can be minced. Chunks are useful for making stews.

Meat Stew

A staple of meat-eating. Meat stew is made with chopped garlic and a mirepoix mix. Cook them in a cooking pot, then add four chunks of meat and some salt. Beef is my favorite, but any good quality meat will do. Cook until browned, then toss in two flasks' worth of water to deglaze, and add some chopped thyme, rosemary, and cooking sage. Bring to a boil, then simmer until reduced and delicious.

Variation: Hunter's Stew

Now we're talkin’! This stew is a great use of the more gamey bushmeats you might find out in the wild. Take four chunks of bushmeat, two flasks of water, some sea salt, chopped sage, and cooking thyme. Throw it all in a pot, and you'll be eating good in no time.

Meat Steaks

Who doesn't like a good steak? Maybe some mewling elven princeling, but we're carnivores here! Take a steak of meat, toss on some salt, and cook over a fire. It's that simple, folks.

Jerky

No hunter would leave home without a trusty bag of jerky. Combine some white vinegar, a cut steak, some sea salt, and some paprika. Roast it
low and slow until it's completely dry.

Now you've got enough knowledge to eat well in the woods. Good luck out there, hunters!

Deep Elf Archers starting in Ail'Vorith start with this item in their inventory. 
You have been spared.

You only exist by the mercy of:

THE ETERNAL QUEEN AND HIGH LISTENER,
QUEEN NALIADRA
The Queen of Corruption, She Who Spoke With
the Shadow, the Immortal Consort of the
Darkness, and the Avatar of Barbhaal

Make no reference to your former house from this point forward, as it never existed.
Therefore, you have no privileged beyond the breath you breathe and your ability to serve
our Queen.

You have been cast out of Ail'vorith, welcome
only in its Foreign Quarter, as befitting one of 
the shadowless. Any attempt to enter further 
districts will result in your immediate 
extermination. You have been warned.

To prove yourself useful to our Queen and the 
Houses of Ail'vorith, seek the head toilmaster 
outside the city. Find him and present to him 
this writ if you wish to be tested for any worth 
left in you.

You are now a shadowless nothing. It is 
your decision as to whether you remain such.

items.name: Szuur's Famous Foods
items.notes:
The culinary secrets of Szuur, revealed to you in this volume!

Our first sample of light fare is the veritable toum, a creamy garlic sauce. The trick is in the emulsification.

   Combine six chopped cloves of garlic with sea salt, and the juice of half a lemon in a mortar and pestle. Add a portion of olive oil - slowly - and grind until it becomes a creamy paste.

Next, we have za'atar, which goes wonderfully on flatbread.

   Chop thyme, oregano and sumac berries, and add sesame seeds, a pinch of sea salt, and some olive oil. Tastes delicious spread on flatbread.

We have falafel. These delicious chickpea balls are shock full of spices and herbs.

   Grind some coriander seed and cumin, add some choppes cilantro, dill, parsley, and garlic, throw in some cayenne peppers, and two helpings of chickpeas. Fry or bake them, and voila! Falafel.

The delicious kebab is a titan of street food in Szuur. Here's how to make them:

   Take some meat - either two portions of minced beef or mutton, or one of each, if you want a doner kebab - and add chopped parsley, white onion, and some ground cumin and cardamom. Sprinkle on some salt, and wrap the meat onto your spit. Cook until well done, and then slice off portions with a knife.

Now, you might be wanting some flatbread to eat with those kebabs.

   Take two portions of wheat dough, roll and stretch them flat. Add some wheat flour if they stick. Bake until golden-brown.

Shakshouka is a wonderful breadfast, make sure to share it with some friends!

   Chop two tomatoes and bell peppers, add some chopped garlic and white onion, a cayenne pepper, and some ground cumin, with paprika in a pot. Bring to a boil, then crack eight chicken eggs. Serve hot.

Dolmas are a delicious snack, and quite portable!

   Halve a lemon, using the juice from one of the halves, and combine with the basmati rice. Wrap them in grape leaves, and drizzle olive oil on top.

Saffron Rice is a staple of food in Szuur. The recipe is very simple.

   Chop a white onion, add some sea salt, and toss it in your pot. Mix some warm water with the saffron and let it sit a moment, before removing the onion and toasting your rice in the hot pan. Re-add the onion and the saffron, cover, and cook for ten minutes.

Finally, there's hummus.

   Take two helpings of chick peas, and mix with ground cumin, sea salt, and the juice of half a lemon. Make sure you use a mixing bowl!

And there you have it: The culinary secrets of Szuur, uncovered!

items.name: The Joy of Surveying
items.notes:
Given by [[Tig Pebblebank]]. It reads : The Joy of Surveying (A Beginners Guide)
by Tig Pebblebank, Lead Measurer of The Measure

Items needed:

Rope: knotted, long enough to cover the distance measured.

Pitons x 2: to mark the spot you want to measure from and the spot you want to measure to.

Hammer: to drive the pitons into the ground.

Parchment: to write down your measurements.

Instrument of marking parchment: This can be charcoal or chalk as they are readily available. However, those who have taken apprenticeship within The Measure will be given their token of apprenticeship, a lead disk, which is much superior to charcoal or chalk as it lasts much longer than the prior instruments.

How to measure length:

Step 1: Find spot you want to measure from.
Step 2: Hammer piton 1 into that spot.
Step 3: Find spot you want to measure to.
Step 4: Hammer piton 2 in that spot.
Step 5: Take knotted rope and place rope on piton 1.
Step 6: Pull the rope toward piton 2 and place rope on the piton once you get there.
Step 7: Count the knots between piton 1 and piton 2.

The sum of the knots is the length between the two pitons. Easy, isn't it?

Notes from the Author:

It is custom of the guild of The Measure to wrap bright green cloth to these pitons in order to be seen clearly from a distance.

Creating a certified knotted rope is covered in the advanced manual “Advanced Rope Techniques”. Please see a Lead Measurer if a knotted rope is needed.

The subject “The History of Length” is covered in the “Measurer’s Almanac”.

There has been some debate among measurers as to whether the act of tying the rope to the piton would be in fact be more practical than just placing the rope on the piton. I assure you dear reader, the act of placing the rope near the piton with the rope held is the correct and cursory way to complete this task quickly.

items.name: Torn Note
items.notes:
This note is given to beginner enchanters in [[Night Harbor]] and starts the [[Enchanter Starter Quest (Night Harbor)|Enchanter Starter Quest]]. 
Do not be startled, , but you have a choice to make, and time is of the essence.

Do you register as a practitioner of mind magic, as the law requires, and face a lifetime of scrutiny and obedience to a faceless bureaucracy?

Or do you maintain your anonymity, seek the aid of like-minded beguilers, and chart your own course?

The choice is yours, though we advise you to pursue the latter.

Deliver this note to Master Wincog at his curious goods shop. You'll find it along the long flight of stairs that connects Sageside to Saltbreeze Park. Look for the sign.
